Hi everyone,

I'm using the pcountOpen to estimate abundance, recruiment and detection of four populations of a crab on isolated oceanic islands.
My data includes counts from 12 sites (the islands have from one to five sites) from 2002-2020 with unequal intervals between primary occasions. For each primary occasion I have 5 secondary occasions, but almost of the year-site observations are missing values.

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] pcountOpen multi-year data with many missing data
parts:
Hi Thais,

 

With counts as high as yours, it can take a very long time to integrate over all possible values of abundance. MCMC can be more computationally efficient in these cases, especially if you will need the posterior distributions for abundance. That said, you have a lot of heterogeneity in your count data, and many missing values, which will be difficult to model regardless of the approach you use. Sorry, wish I had a better answer for you.

 

Richard
